card.name: Sentence-ending points in warning text
card.fires_on: The last word of a clause just before a sentence ends, such as "possible" in "as soon as possible" or a period after a statement of risk. It is mostly found in drug warning text, and also in a physics passage.

modes.label: as soon as possible
modes.description: The word "possible" ending the instruction to discontinue the drug when pregnancy is detected.
modes.example: When pregnancy is detected, discontinue quinapril and hydrochlorothiazide as soon as<< possible>>. These adverse outcomes are usually associated with

modes.label: Period after a stated risk or fact
modes.description: A period closing a sentence about a risk or a physical principle, right before the next sentence starts.
modes.example: SSRIs and SNRIs, including escitalopram oxalate, may increase the risk of bleeding events<<.>> Concomitant use of aspirin,

modes.label: Word ending a warning phrase
modes.description: The final noun or linking word in a set phrase, such as "behavior" in "suicidal thoughts and behavior".
modes.example: WARNING: SUICIDAL THOUGHTS AND BEHAVIORS Antidepressants increased the risk of suicidal thoughts and<< behavior>> in children, adolescents, and young adults

card.plain: It fires at the point where a warning sentence is about to end and a new one is about to begin.
